label: Codex Leicester
summary: Notebook of 18 double sheets (72 pages) on water, the Earth and the Moon, in a private collection (Bill Gates) since 1994.
history: Thomas Coke, later Earl of Leicester, 1717 or 1719

claims.statement: The codex consists of 18 double sheets giving 72 pages.

claims.statement: The first chronology draft gives c.1504 to 1510; no source seen in this session supports a start before 1506.
The Museo Galileo exhibition text records the sculptor Guglielmo della Porta as an early owner; its stated year (1537) is not reconcilable with della Porta's biography without checking.

claims.statement: The painter Giuseppe Ghezzi owned the codex in Rome by 1689 (Museo Galileo) or c.1690 (Italian press).

claims.statement: Thomas Coke, later Earl of Leicester, bought the codex from Ghezzi; sources give 1717 or 1719. It stayed with the family at Holkham for over two centuries.

sources.cite: Fanpage.it, Firenze, il ritorno del Codice da Vinci agli Uffizi in prestito da Bill Gates.
Museo Galileo, exhibition site Water as Microscope of Nature: the Codex Leicester, introduction.

claims.statement: Sold at Christie's, London, on 12 December 1980 to Armand Hammer for about 5.1 million US dollars and renamed Codex Hammer.

sources.cite: HISTORY.com, Da Vinci notebook sells for over 5 million (12 December 1980 sale).

claims.statement: Sold at Christie's, New York, on 11 November 1994 for 30,802,500 US dollars to a buyer later identified as Bill Gates, who restored the name Codex Leicester.

sources.cite: Seattle Times, Codex history, a coveted trophy for the intellectually curious, 14 October 1997.
